elements.element: The cap equals the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: No fees-based cap, 12-month measurement period, USD 1,000,000 floor, or greater-of formula appears.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped for both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause states only that nothing in the relevant Section limits the Servicer’s or Marketing Agent’s liability for confidentiality breaches. It does not provide a mutual carve-out, and Section 9.6 may still restrict recovery against the Depositor or Issuer.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped for both parties.
elements.evidence: Data-protection liability is protected from the relevant Section only for the Servicer and Marketing Agent, not mutually, and the separate limited-recourse provision remains operative.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped for both parties.

result.reason: The operative text does not implement either requested cap structure. It instead retains broad liability waivers and a one-directional limited-recourse restriction, while adding selected one-sided carve-outs for the Servicer and Marketing Agent. The addition of ordinary-negligence liability is not required by either position, so the redline is not minimal. The retained waivers and limited-recourse provision also undermine the intended mutual capped-liability framework. The margin comment cannot cure these operative omissions.
